_frozen: 2026-09-07 setup pass; values fixed BEFORE execution and may not be changed after inspecting any result
_classification_note: Every key is classified: PHYSICAL_INPUT (inherited from the record), NUMERICAL (computational parameter, no physical content), or CONTROL (battery configuration).

physical._m2_note: BARE mass zero: this is the unlifted-zero-mode starting point. Any relaxation in the primary run must be GENERATED by the self-interaction, not supplied.
physical._lambda_note: lambda=0.01 => sqrt(lambda)=0.1 => the record's m_eff^2 = 0.1 H^2 via the SY dynamical-mass rule (RESULTS_conformalon.md). This is the record's own referent value, not a tuned choice.

numerical._class: NUMERICAL -- computational parameters; no physical content; none is a new scale
numerical._fit_windows_note: THREE preregistered windows for the O1b cross-check. Chosen EX ANTE from: (i) the analytic ensemble-mean noise floor sigma_phi/sqrt(N) with sigma_phi from the SY closed-form stationary variance, (ii) the two already-identified candidate rates, and (iii) the predetermined detectability criterion SNR >= 5 at every window end, evaluated against the FASTER candidate (the binding case). No stochastic result existed when these were fixed and none may reopen them.
numerical._ac_note: Autocorrelation route O1a (PRIMARY): 400 stationary trajectories, lags to 150 Hubble times. Stationary averaging has no SNR cliff, which the ensemble-mean decay fit does.
numerical._n_traj_note: 4000. The primary estimator is the stationary autocorrelation, which has no ensemble-mean SNR cliff; n_traj is therefore set by the cross-check windows, which are SNR-safe at 4000 (see _fit_windows_note). Not raised further, to keep the horizon extension affordable.
numerical._t_max_note: 600 Hubble times so the burn-in (50% = 300) exceeds ~2.7 relaxation times of the SLOWER preregistered target (1/k_B = 113): the autocorrelation route requires genuine stationarity for BOTH candidates, not just the faster one. Fixed ex ante from the two candidate rates.
numerical._fit_window_coordinate_note: The O1b decay fit measures relaxation of <phi> FROM THE INITIAL CONDITION, which is a TRANSIENT observable: it must be taken BEFORE the system relaxes, i.e. before burn_in_time. These windows are therefore absolute simulation times in the transient phase and are NOT post-burn-in stationary windows. This is deliberate, not an inconsistency.
numerical._autocorrelation_coordinate_note: The O1a autocorrelation (PRIMARY) is computed in the STATIONARY phase [burn_in_time, t_max] = [300,600]; its tau <= ac_lag_max_t = 200 is a LAG, not an absolute time. The '6.7 / 1.77 e-folds' figures refer to THIS lag range x the two target rates, never to the O1b windows.
numerical._rng_note: Recorded explicitly for cross-environment reproducibility. One Random instance per ensemble run, seeded from seed_list_explicit; draws are consumed in trajectory-index order within each timestep.
numerical._ac_analysis_knobs_note: PREREGISTERED analysis parameters, lifted out of hardcoded Python defaults after a pre-execution audit found they were absent from the frozen config and never inspected by the auditor -- while prereg section 5 classifies every analysis range as a preregistered design decision. ac_fit_frac raised 0.6 -> 0.8 so the EFFECTIVE fitted span exceeds 1 e-fold at the slower target with margin (1.42 rather than 1.06). The fit uses lags with tau <= ac_fit_frac*tau_max AND C/C0 > ac_amplitude_cut, so the EFFECTIVE span is min(ac_fit_frac*tau_max, ln(1/ac_amplitude_cut)/k) -- NOT the full lag range.

tolerances._class: DESIGN DECISION -- declared explicitly for review; frozen before execution
tolerances._note: No defensible threshold exists in the record for these; they are design decisions, stated here rather than hidden in code, and may not be relaxed after seeing results.
tolerances._window_note: max relative spread of the three O1b decay-fit rates. GATING RULE (fixed ex ante): this criterion gates CONVERGED only when the MEASURED rate is fast enough that the windows span >= 1 e-fold; if the measured rate implies < 1 e-fold per window (as target B would: 0.31-0.53), O1b is reported INCONCLUSIVE for that route and does NOT invalidate the O1a primary. Without this rule a legitimate slow-rate result would be failed for a purely statistical reason.
tolerances._precision_note: MEASURED, not guessed. A pre-execution calibration of the PRIMARY estimator on synthetic AR(1) data with an exactly known Lambda, in production geometry, returned bias -1% to +3% and scatter 7-11% (ac_traj 400 -> 1600 improved scatter only 10.1% -> 7.1%, because the error is dominated by ORIGIN CORRELATION -- ~40 highly-correlated origins over a 100-Hubble-time span -- not by trajectory count, so it is not affordably reducible). The previous 5%/15% values were arbitrary design decisions TIGHTER than the instrument's intrinsic precision: they would have made CONVERGED unreachable and branches I-a/I-b unreachable except by luck, on perfectly good data. tol_rate/tol_seed are therefore set to 25% (~3x the measured scatter). THIS IS NOT A WEAKENED TEST: the discrimination the run is FOR is target A vs target B, which are 3.8x (280%) apart -- roughly 30 standard deviations of the measured scatter. What the instrument cannot do is certify a 5% match, and claiming it could was the defect. Control Q2-C11 re-measures this calibration at run time and voids the precision claim if it drifts.
